input.quote: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
input.rationale: The only governing-law/venue provision (§ 20(h)) selects Nova Scotia law and the Nova Scotia courts. Nova Scotia is not among the accepted laws (New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales) and so fails both the preferred and the fallback position on the material terms of governing law and forum. The venue is non-exclusive, which mitigates the walk-away concern of a mandatory foreign forum, but the governing law itself is still outside the approved list. No arbitration clause exists (the only reference to arbitration fees is in the indemnity cost definition at p0090), so no foreign seat issue. We propose the smallest edit reaching the preferred position: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, keeping the rest of the sentence structure intact.

ops.oldText: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
ops.newText: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We moved governing law and venue to our accepted New York position, as Nova Scotia law and courts fall outside our approved list. If helpful, we can accept Delaware, California, or England and Wales (with the courts of London) as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Replace Nova Scotia governing law and venue with New York law and exclusive New York County courts.
